steps.content: [Begin with Black Screen, then transition to Small CG 1]
The Rules of Detective Novels - I. The culprit must be someone who appeared in the story, all the while being someone beyond the reader's expectations.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: "Murder on the Praeva Express" is a story of hatred and fury. It mirrors reality, exposing the truth behind the Redwood fire, and serves as retribution against the arsonist.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Who is the arsonist? I don't know. But while thinking about this, I noticed a contradiction in everything you've said.

options: Why are you so obsessed with all the marketing hype?

steps.content: II. The detective must not solve the case through supernatural or bizarre methods;

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: "A thrilling experience that mirrors reality," "the victim is the author herself," "serialized chapters to build anticipation"... According to you, everything you did was for publicity.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Yet, in your book, those who boarded the Praeva seeking vengeance feel so... vivid, and lovable. You showed them compassion and pity. That doesn't read like you were exploiting their suffering for fame and fortune.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: In that case...

options: Why did you name the victim after yourself?

steps.content:
<color=#ff007f><b><size=45>
III. The crime scene must not have more than one secret room or passageway;

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Who does the victim "Clementine" represent? And, if such a person exists, why not reveal their actual name?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Perhaps you don't know who that person is. Or perhaps... every person who tried to expose that name has already been silenced.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So the author Clementine created a fictional setting, separate from DisCity, and changed the arsonist's name to evade censorship—because only then could the story be published.

options: But then, what's the point of going through all that trouble just to publish this story?

steps.content:
<color=#ff007f><b><size=45>
IV. The detective must not solve cases through coincidences or unfounded intuition,
nor through clues that were never revealed to the reader;

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And the answer is to expose someone who escaped the hammer of justice long ago. Someone even the Chief of MBCC would have trouble investigating.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This book exists to make more people see it, to get more people to talk about it. If the truth has been concealed and twisted, then you simply need to get everyone involved. The public will be the one to pass judgment.

options: At the same time, this ensures that the true culprit will also see it.

steps.content:
<color=#ff007f><b><size=45>
V. The detective must not be the criminal.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The arsonist is protected, hidden in darkness, only striking when someone tries to expose the truth.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You never wrote for money. What you seek is worth far more. Using a <color=#fb9259>fictional train</color> as a disguise, a <color=#fb9259>victim bearing the author's name</color> as your hook, you wrote about a <color=#fb9259>tragedy that truly occurred in Eastside</color>—
[Clementine's portrait]

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Clementine, you are Redwood's last chance at revenge.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You're using yourself as bait to draw out the true culprit, aren't you?
You and Clementine lock eyes for a long moment. Finally, she smiles.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Oh my...
She begins to clap slowly. The sound echoes clearly in the study.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: As expected of the MBCC Chief. Your insight is as sharp as I expected, and you truly are an impressive person. The clues, the motives, and even those deliberately overlooked gaps... you caught them all.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I have nothing to add. It's my loss. You have my complete acknowledgment.

options: ...So you really are a survivor of that fire.

steps.content: "Who is Clementine?" The mystery you've been pursuing from the start has finally been answered, yet it brings you no comfort. After all, far more questions remain unanswered.
Behind those concealed and altered records, what really happened to Redwood Orphanage?

options: What exactly happened after that fire?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: ...You already know the answer, don't you?
Clementine's voice remains calm. One would think she's only recounting someone else's past.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Redwood was an orphanage. It took in children who had no home and sheltered adults with nowhere else to go. For everyone there, Redwood was the only place where they belonged.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: But then... in just a single night, everyone died, and our home was gone. Everything changed after that.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: After the fire, people were sympathetic at first, but that quickly turned into rumors, conspiracy theories, as well as endless speculation. The survivors were dragged out again and again to be scrutinized and questioned. It's like they were convinced that the world could return to peace so long as the blame was pinned on us.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Our benefactors vanished. The insurance company refused to pay, claiming the fire was caused by "improper conduct," and therefore, they could not compensate us.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: As for the sheriff who was first assigned to investigate... He was a good man, but he didn't get far. He was quickly dismissed over some trivial matter and barred from the case entirely.
Clementine pulls out a folder from a drawer beneath the table and hands it to you. You open it to find handwritten records documenting the Redwood fire.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: The original crime scene investigation record, before it was altered. The very first draft.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Can't these notes be used as evidence to reopen the investigation?
Clementine offers a faint smile. The answer to your question, you realize, is painfully obvious.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Of course, we tried to appeal. But every complaint we filed went unanswered, and the investigation into the fire was shut down, swept under the rug. Eventually, Redwood's very existence was dismissed as nothing more than some ridiculous urban legend.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: That's when we all realized... none of this was a coincidence.
She lowers her gaze, her gloved fingertips tracing the words on the page.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: The one who left that cigarette butt erased the evidence, twisted the truth, and hid behind their power... clearing themself of any sin.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This was the only way for you to expose the truth.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The culprit hides behind layers of power and privilege. They only act when they need to conceal information about the fire.
This is the truth Clementine seeks to expose. If the law won't hold them accountable, then public opinion will.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But what if it doesn't work? What if they see the public outcry and simply choose not to act? Then—
You stop mid-sentence. There's something in Clementine's expression as she looks at you. In that moment, a different possibility dawns on you.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I think the fact that you were sent here says enough, wouldn't you agree?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The Intelligence Department traced the letter back to a public IP in Eastside. We couldn't identify the sender. Now I see why...
Your arrival here was no coincidence. Clementine knew her plan had worked the moment you walked through that door.
If reality forbids her from speaking plainly, then she will speak through stories. Even if her voice is silenced, she needs only to preserve the evidence in ink.
Her vengeance began the moment her first novel was published. At this point, it's already too late for anyone to stop it.
But...
After you find the arsonist, then what? What are you planning to do? Stab them twelve times like in "Praeva"?
What if they come after you first? If they have connections within the Public Security Bureau, they can easily find out everything about you. Using yourself as bait like this is far too dangerous...

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: What else am I supposed to do?
Clementine cuts you off. Her voice remains calm, though you catch a faint trace of sorrow beneath it.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: If everything in this book is real...

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: If, one day, the law fails to punish the wicked, and there's no one left to uphold justice... If someone is denied every avenue of appeal and chooses to seek retribution through such extreme methods...

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Would you shield us? Or would you uphold the law and see to it that we face the consequences we deserve?

options: Lynching will only make things worse.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The MBCC only handles threats involving Sinners and Mania. Other cases fall outside my jurisdiction. So, whatever you choose to do, I won't interfere.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And if you still can't let this go, then... I want you to wait for me, at the very least.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: There's only so much I can do as the Chief of the MBCC, but I know plenty of people from all walks of life who'd be willing to help. Now that I know the truth, I'm certain they won't hesitate to lend a hand.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'll investigate this with you. We'll find the person responsible and make them answer for what they've done. We can be the voice for those who were denied the justice they deserve.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And if you can't hold yourself back when we find them... feel free to rough them up a little.
You recall a time when you, too, were overtaken by anger—leaving a certain blonde Fraser individual with more than a few bruises around their eyes.

options: It's not like I've never done something like that. I'll keep it between us.

steps.content: You can see Clementine's surprise in her eyes, followed by a trace of melancholy. Then, as you make that final remark, she couldn't help but laugh.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Good deeds are rewarded, and evil receives its due...

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: If only a world like that exists outside of stories.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: We'll make it a reality.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So... promise me you won't do anything reckless. There's no need to stain your hands.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Thank you, ${PlayerName}.
Clementine offers a gentle smile.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: What I hoped for when I wrote those words... was that perhaps one day, outside the pages of a story, I'd hear someone say them in the real world too.
And after you've taken your revenge? How will you handle the Public Security Bureau's investigation? How will you deal with the retaliation from the forces backing them?
There's only so much a handful of people can do. Even with a Sinner's power, you'd be hard-pressed to stand against a family that's been entrenched in Eastside for decades.
Clementine's smile becomes slightly bitter. Your words are blunt, but you both understand that's the reality.

I know this type of case falls outside MBCC's jurisdiction, but at the end of the day, I still hold an official position. With my authority as Chief, I'll have far more protection than you do, and I can access leads you couldn't reach.
Besides, I know plenty of people from all walks of life who'd be eager to help. They're the type who can't say no to a good cause. I'm certain they won't hesitate to lend a hand.
I'll investigate. I'll find the person responsible and bring them before you. I'll make them answer for what they've done, and be the voice for those who were denied the justice they deserve.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: ...Right.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Good deeds are rewarded, and evil receives its due... If only that were true.
Once you get blood on your hands, there's no going back. I don't want you to destroy yourselves by going down that path.
So... wait for me. Don't do anything reckless. Don't stain your hands.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Thank you, ${PlayerName}.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: What I hoped for when I wrote those words... was that perhaps one day, outside the pages of a story, I'd hear someone say them in the real world too.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I hope that this time... justice will really come.
The clock chimes. It's nearly midnight. Your terminal rings at the same time.

<color=#fb9259>Nightingale</color>: Chief, the Intelligence Department has tracked down a new lead.

<color=#fb9259>Nightingale</color>: Based on the name Inspector Doyle provided, we've identified a sheriff who once handled the Redwood case before being transferred to a satellite town. He recently retired and returned to DisCity. The address has been confirmed—we can move at any moment.

<color=#fb9259>${PlayerName}</color>: Good. Wait for me. I'll handle this personally.
When you look back up, you find Clementine watching you quietly, as if she already knows what you're about to say.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: A new lead just came in. I found a sheriff who handled the case. With him in the picture, we might be able to track down the bastard behind all this.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Every investigation is a race against time. I've got to take my leave now, but before I go...
You reach out and raise your pinky finger.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Remember the promise between the detective and Clementine in your book? Those three articles.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You're standing in the spotlight, but your enemy is hiding in the shadows, ready to put you in danger at any moment. The team I'm leaving behind will protect you. Your safety matters more than anything else.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'll bring you the results of the investigation by tomorrow morning. So...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I want you to trust me. At least... wait for me to come back.
A finger hooks onto your pinky and gently shakes it.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: ...Alright. I trust you.
She releases your hand and steps closer, gathering all of her manuscripts and placing them into the folder you're holding.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: You've gathered all the clues. You'll be fine even without me.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: There's no point in my keeping this. Consider it your reward for clearing the challenge.
With all her lies cast aside, her expression softens. You can't help but imagine that perhaps, at some point in the past... this is what Clementine was like, when she still lived in Redwood.
But the past is the past. You need to leave now. There's much to be done—filing clues, deploying personnel to reopen the investigation, and so on. A long list of tasks awaits you.
...But just as you're about to leave, you can't help but call out to her again.

options: What about the other survivors besides you?

steps.content: Those characters in your books... are they also real? Did they really... kill people, just like in the stories?
Clementine pauses for a moment, but she quickly puts on a smile again.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Did you look into it? You couldn't find anything, could you? It's only natural, they're just characters I made up, after all.
Clementine smiles, but it only makes you uneasy.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Don't worry, I intend to keep our promise. As I said, the book was nothing more than a work of fiction from the very start.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: As for who the real culprit is, and how they should be punished...

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I'll leave that to you.
You feel a pull on your wrist. Someone draws you forward, and then something soft brushes tenderly against your ear.
A gentle kiss lands near your ear.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Thank you. I'm glad...

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: In the end... someone understood my true story.
The door closes. Clementine's figure disappears behind it.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Goodbye, my dear detective.
